biography.plain_text: Augusto Reitano is an Italian property developer and hotelier from Messina. His businesses extended from Rome and Milan to New York, where he led Patmos Fifth Real Estate. That company bought a Manhattan redevelopment site in 2006 using mortgage finance. The project later became embroiled in lengthy litigation over debt and foreclosure.

long_biography.plain_text:
Augusto Reitano entered a Milan redevelopment when architect Francesco Mauri needed more money to turn a former industrial site into homes. Joining the venture, he brought in other investors and took responsibility for constructing a streetfront apartment building and two rows of villas. The partners later received properties corresponding to their stakes. In 2005, his Assisi Immobiliare sold fourteen apartments there to a partner's company.

His hospitality interests included Villa Mon Repos in Taormina, a boutique hotel occupying a nineteenth-century house overlooking the sea. By 2016, he also owned Piccola Cucina on Miami Beach's Espanola Way.
